Q1: Zinc oxide has a hazard profile with several known dangers (Tier 1) including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental toxicity (ENV), and organ/systemic effects (OGN) according to the Globally Harmonized System. Further review (Tier 2) indicates potential inhalation (IHL) and dermal/eye (SKN) hazards. While oral exposure (ORL) is classified as a low-to-moderate hazard (Tier 3), there is insufficient data to confidently assess its endocrine disruption potential (EDC Tier 4).
Q2: Zinc oxide is listed on the TEDX (The Endocrine Disruption Exchange) list as a potential endocrine disruptor, based on scientific evidence. This listing highlights a specific area of concern, aligning with the chemical's Tier 4 (data deficient) classification for endocrine disruption hazards.
Q3: Zinc oxide is extensively characterized, evidenced by a very high number of scientific literature references (419,000) and a precisely defined molecular formula (OZn) as a small molecule. Despite a specific data gap in its endocrine disruption potential (EDC Tier 4), the overall depth of study suggests a robust understanding of many of its other hazard characteristics.
